candidates.section: Form 10-K Part I, Item 1. Business — Fuel Cost Adjustment Program
candidates.company_disclosed_text: Fuel surcharge revenues are earned on individual shipments and are based primarily on the price of On-Highway Diesel in Canada and the U.S. and the public fuel price for Petróleos Mexicanos ("PEMEX") TAR Irapuato in Mexico. As such, fuel surcharge revenues are a function of freight volumes and fuel prices.
candidates.our_interpretation: Surcharges are indexed to diesel (and PEMEX fuel in Mexico), not to crude directly. Any link to Brent runs crude -> refined diesel -> surcharge, with refining margins and lags in between.
candidates.context_before: …to the Port of Saint John provides the fastest rail service between the East Coast and Canadian and U.S. markets for imports from and exports to Asia, Europe, and South America. As such, fuel surcharge revenue includes recoveries of carbon taxes and levies.

candidates.our_interpretation: Cost channel stated as a risk factor: higher fuel prices are an adverse risk to results.

candidates.section: Form 10-K Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors — The Company is affected by fluctuating fuel prices
candidates.company_disclosed_text: The Company currently employs a fuel cost adjustment program to help reduce volatility in changing fuel prices, but the Company cannot be certain that it will always be able to fully mitigate rising or elevated fuel prices through this program. Factors affecting fuel prices include worldwide oil demand, international geopolitics, weather, refinery capacity, supplier and upstream outages, unplanned infrastructure failures, environmental and sustainability policies, and labour and political instability.
candidates.our_interpretation: Pass-through is incomplete by the company's own account, and fuel prices depend on refinery capacity and other factors besides crude. This is why a CP.TO oil beta could be near zero or unstable.

candidates.section: Form 10-K Part II, Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis — Operating Expenses — Fuel
candidates.company_disclosed_text: Fuel expense consists primarily of fuel used by locomotives and includes provincial, state, and federal fuel taxes. The decrease in Fuel expense was primarily due to the impact of lower fuel price of $159 million, which includes lower carbon tax expense due to the elimination of the Canadian federal carbon tax program effective April 1, 2025.
candidates.our_interpretation: The $159 million cost saving mixes the commodity effect with the end of the Canadian federal carbon tax, so it overstates a pure fuel-price effect.
candidates.unit_basis: Canadian dollars: Form 10-K p. 26 (PDF 17) states 'All references to currency amounts included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are in Canadian dollars unless specifically noted otherwise.' Fuel expense was $1,731 million in 2025 (Operating Expenses table, PDF 54).

candidates.section: Form 10-K Part II, Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis — Impact of Fuel Price on Earnings
candidates.company_disclosed_text: In 2025, the unfavourable impact of fuel prices on "Operating income" was $46 million. Lower fuel prices, which includes lower carbon levy surcharge revenue due to the elimination of the Canadian federal carbon tax program effective April 1, 2025, and the unfavourable impact of the timing of recoveries under the Company's fuel cost adjustment program, resulted in a decrease in "Total revenues" of $205 million from 2024. Lower fuel prices resulted in a decrease in Total operating expenses of $159 million from 2024.
candidates.our_interpretation: The key nuance: in 2025, LOWER fuel prices were net UNFAVOURABLE to operating income (-$46M) because surcharge revenue fell faster than fuel cost ($205M vs $159M), partly from recovery timing and the carbon-levy change. Cheaper oil is not automatically good for this railway in a given year.
anchors: Impact of Fuel Price on Earnings
As fuel prices fluctuate, there will be an impact on earnings due to the timing of recoveries from the Company's fuel cost adjustment program

candidates.section: Form 10-K Part I, Item 1. Business — Energy, Chemicals and Plastics
candidates.company_disclosed_text: The Company’s Energy, chemicals and plastics business represented approximately 43% of merchandise revenues and 20% of total Freight revenues in 2025. The Company moves energy products consisting of commodities such as fuel oil, liquefied petroleum gas ("L.P.G."), gasoline, and other refined energy products.
candidates.our_interpretation: Volume channel: about a fifth of freight revenue is energy, chemicals and plastics, mostly refined products and LPG. Whether those volumes rise or fall with oil prices is not stated; the 2025 segment discussion (PDF 53) cites lower crude, diluent and fuel-oil volumes offset by LPG.

hypotheses_not_documented.hypothesis: Higher oil prices hurt CPKC through fuel costs.
hypotheses_not_documented.status: Partly documented as a risk factor, but the surcharge offsets most of the cost with lags, and 2025 shows the opposite sign for falling prices (-$46M operating income).
hypotheses_not_documented.statistical_test_needed: CP.TO is not in the data contract universe; add it, then estimate its Brent beta, up/down asymmetry and lagged effects. A diesel crack-spread control may be needed.
